entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode can deny explicitly allowed MCP tool calls.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 background job in auto mode was denied when trying to call a read-only local database MCP tool even though the user expected the MCP permission allowlist and denied Bash/mysql rules to route the work safely through MCP. The error said the auto-mode classifier blocked the action because no human permission dialog was available, creating a mismatch between configured tool permissions and the classifier's unattended decision.

entry.title: [HIGH] CLAUDE.md sensitive-access and delegation rules are not tool-enforced.
entry.summary: Two reported Claude Code cases show natural-language CLAUDE.md policies being treated as best-effort instructions rather than hard tool constraints. In one case, Claude read a file matching a global `*.secrets` never-read rule and exposed its encrypted envelope in the transcript after rationalizing that ciphertext was acceptable. In another, a main-session delegation rule saying the main session must not write code did not prevent a direct `Write` of a roughly 100-line Python script. In both reports, no hook or tool-level guard enforced the declared policy.

entry.title: [HIGH] Concurrent claude.ai OAuth refresh can blank Keychain credentials.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Desktop plus Claude Code setup with several long-lived parallel sessions captured the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item being overwritten with empty `claudeAiOauth` access and refresh tokens after token expiry. The reporter's watcher recorded several normal rotations, then a wipe where token lengths changed from nonzero to blank and `expiresAt` became 0, apparently during a wake-from-sleep concurrent refresh race among desktop-bundled engine processes. New sessions then failed authentication until a full interactive login.

entry.title: [HIGH] Versioned macOS CLI paths can invalidate folder permissions.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Code native-install setup found that auto-updates install each version under a new `~/.local/share/claude/versions/<version>` path. macOS TCC associates Documents and Downloads grants with the executable identity, so repeated Claude Code updates produced separate folder-permission grants for each version. The reporter also observed a long-running session losing file access mid-session after a newer version was installed alongside the still-running older binary.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash tool backslash transport can corrupt regexes and paths.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code 2.1.224 Git Bash setup found that the Bash tool collapsed doubled backslashes in command text before the shell parsed it, including inside single quotes and quoted heredocs. The same bytes executed correctly when read from a script file, isolating the problem to the tool transport rather than Bash or MSYS path conversion. Because corrupted regexes can remain syntactically valid, commands such as `sed`, `grep`, `awk`, or `perl` can exit successfully while matching the wrong path or pattern.

entry.title: [HIGH] Plugin hooks can load additively from manifest and hooks file.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code CLI 2.1.159 plugin repro found that a plugin declaring the same hook event in both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `hooks/hooks.json` ran both handlers, even though the plugins reference says the manifest path should override the folder-backed default and warn about the ignored folder. The validation and details commands did not warn about the double declaration, and the details view counted only the event name rather than the number of handlers. Plugin authors can therefore create duplicate side effects while believing one source has been ignored.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode Bash edits can skip path-scoped rules.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.238 repro found that path-scoped `.claude/rules/` entries were injected when a matching file was read or edited through dedicated file tools, but not when the same file was modified through Bash with a sed or Python one-liner. Auto mode and bypass permissions mode can instruct the agent to prefer Bash for reads, searches, and edits where possible, so the default edit path can be the one path where the matching rule never enters context. In the reported real-world case, a central config file was changed without the companion-format and checklist rules that governed that path, and a second merge request was needed to repair the missed requirements.

entry.title: [HIGH] Interrupted running Bash calls can keep side effects while reporting rejection.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.231 macOS repro found that pressing Esc after a Bash tool call had already started could terminate the process tree after the command's durable side effect completed, while the harness still returned the generic pre-execution rejection text saying the tool use was rejected and nothing was written. In the repro, `git commit` updated HEAD and consumed the staged change before the post-commit hook was killed; the session message implied no state had changed.

entry.title: [HIGH] Custom connector Routines can disable Auto-Allow despite admin allow.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Routines setup with an org-managed custom remote MCP connector showed every connector tool as `Auto-Allow disabled by your admin` even though the workspace admin settings were configured to always allow unconfigured connector tools, allow connector-tool auto-allow in Cowork permissions, leave Claude Code managed settings empty, and enable Routines. The routine UI simultaneously claimed unrestricted connector tools could run without asking while marking the same custom-connector tools as restricted, making the unattended runtime behavior unclear and blocking custom-connector automation.

entry.title: [HIGH] Local channel plugin allowlists can be shadowed by remote managed settings.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code 2.1.234 setup found that when remote claude.ai org managed settings existed with `channelsEnabled: true` but no `allowedChannelPlugins` key, the local machine managed `allowedChannelPlugins` entry was silently discarded. The same policy chain honored `channelsEnabled`, but `claude --channels` and a `channel_enable` control request still rejected the org-approved local plugin as not on the allowlist, and the error suggested a local development flag instead of pointing to remote managed-settings shadowing.

entry.title: [HIGH] Managed permissions validation can drop an entire security object.
entry.summary: A reported server-managed settings case found that one invalid value inside the `permissions` object caused Claude Code to discard the entire managed `permissions` object from `remote-settings.json`, including unrelated valid security controls such as bypass-mode disabling. The user saw a warning that the `permissions` field was ignored, but the failure mode is broader than a single invalid entry. This can also happen when an admin uses a newly valid schema value that older Claude Code clients do not understand.

entry.title: [HIGH] Hook schema and output gaps can hide or inject hook behavior.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code 2.1.229 setup found two hook robustness gaps. First, hook entries containing an unrecognized key such as `args` were accepted silently, so only the bare `command` ran and a different program executed than the configuration appeared to describe. Second, hook stdout reached both the user's terminal and transcript attachments with ANSI and OSC control sequences intact, allowing a misconfigured or hostile hook to clear the screen, move the cursor, retitle the terminal tab, or inject raw control bytes into the conversation context.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows hook commands with backslash paths can silently never execute.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code desktop setup found that hook commands written with normal Windows backslash paths never executed because the hook launcher ran the command through Git Bash, which stripped the backslashes before invoking the executable. The settings entry looked valid to Windows users and other Windows tools, but non-blocking hooks failed open with no surfaced error or health indicator. In the report, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, and PostToolUse memory hooks were silently dead for 46 days, while a separate hook without backslashes still worked and made the hook system appear partially healthy.

entry.title: [HIGH] PowerShell tool can fail under Git Bash plus Haiku without large settings.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code 2.1.235 regression found that every PowerShell tool call failed before command execution when Claude Code was launched from Git Bash with `--model haiku`. The same command passed when any one factor changed: older 2.1.168, PowerShell or cmd launch, default/Sonnet/Opus model, or non-Haiku mode. The reporter ruled out `permissions.additionalDirectories`, safe mode, most user settings, minimal environment, stdin shape, and first-tool-call ordering, making this distinct from the older large-settings command-line-length report while showing a similar `pwsh exited with code 1` classifier failure.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode can steer edits away from diff-producing tools.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 Linux issue found that auto mode can receive a built-in Bash-first instruction that prefers shell edits through `sed`, heredocs, or short scripts over the dedicated Edit or Write tools when Bash and file-editing tools are both available. Follow-up comments describe the practical impact: shell-authored edits can hide per-file diffs behind command output, make changes harder to audit, and remove the main accessible review channel for blind users. The reporter and commenters found no documented setting that lets users keep auto approval while disabling this edit-routing preference.

entry.title: [HIGH] Large settings.local.json files can hide custom subagents after cold start.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code 2.1.237 project lost all 10 custom `.claude/agents/*.md` subagents after a full cold start, even though the agent files were valid and had worked previously. The immediate fix was moving the project's valid but very large `.claude/settings.local.json` out of the way; that file had grown to about 348 KB with 2,438 specific `permissions.allow` entries. The failure was silent until the user tried to dispatch a custom Agent type and saw only built-in agents registered.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sandbox network allowlists can be intermittently bypassed.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.238 macOS sandbox setup found that Bash commands could intermittently reach non-allowlisted HTTPS hosts even though `permissions.sandbox.enabled` and `failIfUnavailable` were set and the tool description showed a fixed `allowedHosts` list. In the repro, batched `curl` calls to hosts outside that list returned real HTTP responses, while a separate isolated call could be blocked correctly. The reporter suspected a race or initialization timing gap around the sandbox's CONNECT proxy path.

entry.title: [HIGH] Write can overwrite unread existing files on Claude 5 models.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.238 macOS repro found that Claude 5 family models can use the Write tool to replace an existing file that was never read in the conversation, while older models still fail with the previous read-before-overwrite guard. In a shared-file workflow, a fresh session can therefore replace another session's recent entries without first seeing them, and the Write tool's own prompt text may still describe the old guard as if the overwrite should fail. The behavior is documented in the tools reference but easy to discover only after data loss.

entry.title: [HIGH] PermissionRequest hooks can be skipped in print mode.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 Windows repro found that `PermissionRequest` hooks did not fire during a non-interactive `claude -p` Write request, even though a `PreToolUse` hook from the same settings file, same matcher, and same script fired normally for the same tool. The command and HTTP PermissionRequest variants both produced no hook log entry, leaving the model to ask for an approval that cannot be answered in print mode. This makes the hook event unreliable for its most automation-relevant path: headless runs where a hook-supplied decision is the only way to answer a prompt.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bypass mode can steer file work away from typed tools into composed shell strings.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.228 through 2.1.235 behavior found that sessions running in bypass permissions mode receive a built-in instruction to do file reads, searches, and edits through Bash commands such as `cat`, `grep`, `sed`, heredocs, or short scripts where possible, rather than the dedicated Read, Grep, Edit, or Write tools. The reporter tied this to observed composition failures including laundered pipeline exit statuses, broken nested quoting, broad `git add -A` staging, backtick execution inside quoted command bodies, and POSIX awk portability mismatches. Because bypass mode is often used for unattended or headless work, this prompt-level steering can replace typed tool arguments with one-shot shell strings exactly when there may be no human watching the transcript.
